speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is great news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, I notice you are here for a new movement disorder; could you describe the specific involuntary movements you are experiencing and when they first began?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Those symptoms of restlessness and the inability to sit still are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. To confirm this clinical assessment, I will proceed with the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
